purpose: Machine-readable ROKO v1.3 economics facts for simulation consumers.

whitepaper.title: ROKO Network Whitepaper public-release draft v1.3

facts.summary: Mainnet runtime block time is compiled at 3 seconds.
facts.simulation_use: Canonical mainnet v1.3 scenarios should use 3-second blocks unless explicitly modeling testnet or historical calibration.

facts.summary: Current testnet runtime block time is 2 seconds.
facts.simulation_use: Use only for current testnet calibration; do not present as the mainnet assumption.
whitepaper_references: Section 5: testnet versus mainnet transition context

facts.summary: A 6-second production-testnet value is documented as a target, while code currently runs testnet at 2 seconds.
facts.simulation_use: Use as a sensitivity case or planned production-testnet scenario, not as current chain state.
whitepaper_references: Section 5: testnet versus mainnet transition context

facts.summary: Substrate transaction fees and tips are split 20% Treasury, 50% block author, and 30% TemporalFeePool in both runtimes.
facts.simulation_use: Canonical non-EVM fee routing baseline for v1.3 simulations.

value.fallback: current block author receives the pool when no weights exist

facts.summary: TemporalFeePool funds are periodically distributed to timestamping validators by recorded weights, with a block-author fallback.
facts.simulation_use: Model TemporalFeePool as a separate quality/timestamper incentive ledger, not as generic treasury revenue.

facts.summary: EVM gas pricing uses pallet-base-fee with a 1 gwei default base fee and a 75,000,000 block gas limit.
facts.simulation_use: EVM demand scenarios should model gas/base-fee behavior separately from Substrate extrinsic fees.

value.simulation_caveat: Mainnet EVM fees must not be assumed to follow the 20/50/30 DealWithFees split until implementation is changed or confirmed.

facts.summary: EVM fee routing differs between runtimes: testnet routes through DealWithFees, while mainnet currently does not.
facts.simulation_use: Run EVM fee revenue as a caveated or sensitivity path, not as confirmed mainnet Treasury/TemporalFeePool revenue.

facts.summary: pwROKO is minted by reserving native ROKO 1:1, is non-transferable, and unlocks through a two-step cooldown flow.
facts.simulation_use: Enforce 1:1 backing and non-transferability as hard invariants in governance/staking scenarios.

facts.summary: Staking is denominated in pwROKO in both testnet and mainnet runtimes.
facts.simulation_use: Governance power and staking exposure should be modeled through backed pwROKO, not transferable native ROKO balances.

value.reward_asset: native ROKO backing minted and reserved
value.pwroko_issuance: equal pwROKO minted only with direct backing

facts.summary: Staking rewards are minted with direct native backing: the wrapper mints native ROKO, reserves it, records reward-locked backing, and mints equal pwROKO.
facts.simulation_use: Reward compounding must preserve full backing; do not model unbacked pwROKO issuance.
whitepaper_references: Section 7.2: reward payment and pwROKO backing

facts.summary: Staking inflation follows a Substrate reward curve bounded from 2.5% to 10%, with 50% ideal stake and 5% falloff.
facts.simulation_use: Use the curve as the canonical L1 reward model; fixed reward pools should be separate temporary incentive scenarios.

facts.value: no bridge or wrap mechanism exists in the node repo
facts.summary: The runtime repository does not currently include a bridge or wrap mechanism for the Ethereum ERC-20 ROKO contract.
facts.simulation_use: Treat legacy ERC-20 migration as a planned governance/product process until a bridge contract or pallet is added.
code_evidence: repo-wide grep for 6f222e04 across .rs/.md/.json/.ts/.js returns zero matches

contradictions.simulation_resolution: Run 3s as canonical mainnet, 2s for current testnet calibration, and 6s only as a planned-production-testnet sensitivity.

status_map.current: runtime stakes with pwROKO in both runtimes
status_map.stale: README/network table claim that mainnet staking currency is native ROKO

contradictions.simulation_resolution: Model staking and governance power through backed pwROKO; native ROKO is the lock/backing asset.

status_map.planned_or_unresolved: mainnet EVM fee routing must be verified before claiming 20/50/30 EVM fee distribution

contradictions.simulation_resolution: Split Substrate fee routing from EVM fee-routing assumptions; make mainnet EVM fee capture a caveated sensitivity until resolved.

status_map.current: runtime staking rewards follow the 2.5%-10% inflation curve
status_map.stale_or_scenario_only: fixed pre-allocated reward pool as canonical L1 issuance

contradictions.simulation_resolution: Use inflation as canonical L1 security issuance and reserve fixed pools for temporary treasury/incentive programs.

status_map.current: no ERC-20 bridge/wrap path exists in the node repo
status_map.planned: migration requires a separate one-way bridge or governance process if adopted

contradictions.simulation_resolution: Model holder migration as a planned adoption/cutover process until implementation evidence exists.
